newsitem.title: INDIA: India heading for record spices exports in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: India heading for record spices exports in 96/97.

text.p: India is heading for record spices exports in 1996/97 (April-March) with export earnings crossing the 10-billion-rupee ($279 million) mark, state officials said on Tuesday.
"The current year is a milestone in the history of India's spices exports," said an official of the state-run Spices Board, who asked not to be identified.
India exported 193,205 tonnes of spices worth 10.17 billion rupees between April 1996 and February 1997 compared with 175,120 tonnes worth 6.76 billion rupees in the same period a year earlier.
India exported 190,830 tonnes of spices worth 7.43 billion in 1995/96. The Spices Board has set an export target of 195,800 tonnes for 1996/97.

"For the first time earnings from spices exports have crossed the 10-billion-rupee mark. The target in terms of quantity and value for exports for the year is expected to surpass last year's levels," the board official said.
He said: "Our achievement this year was mainly due to the high export of pepper, value added spices shipments through curry powder, mint oil, spices oils and oleoresins."

In the current year, exports of pepper, ginger, coriander, cumin, celery, fennel, garlic, curry powder, mint oil, spices oil and oleoresins increased both in volume and value terms compared with exports in the same period a year ago.
India exported 41,500 tonnes of pepper worth 3.51 billion rupees between April 1996 and February 1997 against 21,663 tonnes worth 1.63 billion rupees in the same period a year earlier.
"India's pepper is in good demand all over and of late in the United States," said T.A. Kuruvilla, a leading spices exporter.
The Spices Board has set a pepper export target of 35,000 tonnes worth 2.45 billion rupees in 1996/97.
"Already this has been exceeded," said Kuruvilla.
India exported 23,800 tonnes of pepper worth 1.8 billion rupees in 1995/96.
